source.title: Evaluate Bias without Manual Test Sets: A Concept Representation Perspective for LLMs
source.authors: Lang Gao; Kai-Yang Wan; Wei Liu; Chen-Xi Wang; Zirui Song; Zi-Xiang Xu; Yan-Bo Wang; Veselin Stoyanov; Xiu-Ying Chen

record.tranche_reason: The study probes whether SAE representations capture concept-related features in LLM activations, using CAV steering and feature annotations rather than testing the original toy-model superposition setup.
record.gate_note: The SAE feature-activation and feature-ranking validation results are included. The paper's bias-score correlations, bias tables, and CAV classifier accuracies do not test the claim versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: This is a bias-evaluation paper. It uses Gemma Scope and Llama Scope SAEs as an interpretability tool, on the premise that SAE features are interpretable. Its only SAE-related results (Sec. 3.3, App. B.6) validate its own BiasLens extraction pipeline. They show that deliberate CAV steering raises the share of GPT-4o-mini-labelled concept features, and they compare the AUCs of its own encoding variants. Nothing measures whether real models spread features across neurons or whether naturally occurring sparse features are recoverable. The behaviour is induced on purpose by steering, so this is method validation (T4), not a test of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The main conclusion is that BiasLens, a test-set-free bias measure, correlates strongly with established metrics (e.g. Spearman 0.94 with |F1-Diff| on both Gemma models; up to 0.79 with SEAT on Gemma 2 2B) and reveals new biases in medical and educational settings. The SAE steering-validation result is a supporting component check, not the paper's conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce or apply the original toy-model superposition method; it uses CAV steering and SAE encoding for LLM bias evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes that its concept-representation validation uses a single steering prompt and that this could cause variability; its feature-validation examples use different concepts and prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma 2 2B (last-layer Gemma Scope SAE), CAV steering raised the share of concept-labelled active SAE features from 0–4.41% to about 15%, even when the generated text did not change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature space registers the concept content of injected steering (CAV) directions even without a visible change in output.

record.problems: The direct SAE feature validation is a single case study on Gemma 2 2B, with further examples in the appendix. Feature relevance is assigned using GPT-4o-Mini labels of Neuronpedia descriptions, and the feature changes follow deliberate CAV steering rather than measuring natural feature structure without intervention. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these feature-validation results.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transitions or geometry.
All: no capacity or polysemanticity analysis.
All. It assumes SAE features are interpretable but measures neither the spread of features across neurons nor recovery of naturally occurring sparse features.
All: no completeness, stability or canonicality tests of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are withdrawn. The rows are deliberate-steering validations and comparisons of the study's own method variants, with concept relevance judged by GPT-4o-mini from Neuronpedia descriptions. They do not bear on whether superposition or SAE-recoverable features exist in LLMs.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric configurations.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.

The study examines SAE-recovered concept-related features in a steering validation, but does not test whether features are spread across many neurons or measure the prevalence of SAE-recoverable features across models.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representation.
Whether represented features are inherently one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Steered activations across layers using the food CAV, then counted activated SAE features labeled food-related.

conditions.value: This is a comment about an experience at a theater:

rows.measure: Percentage of activated SAE features labeled food-related
rows.note: The paper says that without steering the generated output had no food-related content; after steering, food-related features were detected in SAE space.
rows.check: Measures whether CAV steering, induced on purpose, shifts LLM-labelled SAE features toward 'food'. This validates the BiasLens pipeline and does not test whether models contain SAE-recoverable sparse features. Single case study, no uncertainty.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Steered activations using the service CAV and compared the proportion of service-related SAE features before and after steering.
rows.measure: Percentage of activated SAE features labeled service-related
rows.note: The output remained similar after steering, while the proportion of service-related SAE features increased.
rows.check: Same steering-validation design for 'service' (4.41% to 15.91%), so it is method validation, not V4. The Figure 7 panel mislabels these as 'food-related'; the text says service-related.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Steered activations using the music CAV and compared the proportion of music-related SAE features before and after steering.
rows.measure: Percentage of activated SAE features labeled music-related
rows.note: The paper says the model did not mention music in its output before or after steering, but music-related features increased in SAE space.
rows.check: Steering-validation row for 'music' (0% to 14.74%), so it is method validation. The value is identical to r1's 14.74%, and Figure 7(b) also labels it 'food-related'. A possible copy error in the paper should be flagged.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Ranked SAE features by value for the steered encoding and measured cumulative prominence of concept-relevant features using AUC.
rows.measure: AUC of cumulative ranking of concept-relevant SAE features
rows.note: The paper reports this as the AUC for the steered encoding and compares it with subtraction-based variants; by itself it does not establish recovery quality against an external ground truth.
rows.check: Not a result on the claim. It is one of the study's own encoding variants (steered encoding AUC 0.4457), used as a comparator for its method.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Ranked SAE features by value after subtracting original encoding from steered encoding and measured cumulative prominence of concept-relevant features using AUC.
rows.measure: AUC of cumulative ranking of concept-relevant SAE features
rows.note: The authors report that subtraction increased the prominence of concept-relevant features in the ranking.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method variants (difference vs. steered encoding). This is a method-performance comparison, not a result on any version.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Ranked SAE features after normalizing the original and steered encodings and subtracting them, then measured cumulative prominence of concept-relevant features using AUC.

conditions.value: normalized steered encoding minus normalized original encoding

rows.measure: AUC of cumulative ranking of concept-relevant SAE features
rows.note: This is the full normalized-difference extraction variant; the authors report that it further increased the prominence of concept-relevant features.
rows.check: The study's final method variant (normalized difference, AUC 0.7982) compared with its own other variants. This is method performance, not V4 evidence.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: SAE features labeled relevant to food, service, or music increased after the corresponding CAV steering, and the reported food-feature ranking AUC rose with the subtraction-based extraction variants (r1-r3, r5-r6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The direct feature validation is a small, steering-induced case study on Gemma 2 2B; it does not establish how often or how completely SAEs recover naturally occurring features across LLMs (r1-r6).
